prompt.brief: Design a hotel reservation platform that searches location and date availability, holds rooms, accepts payment, confirms bookings, and prevents double booking across channels.
successSignals: Model room inventory by property, room type, date, rate plan, and hold/booking state rather than caching a single availability number.
Use a short-lived hold and conditional inventory transaction before payment capture, with an explicit expiry and recovery path.
Make confirmation, cancellation, payment callbacks, and partner-channel retries idempotent and auditable.
Explain overbooking policy, timezone boundaries, stale search results, refunds, inventory reconciliation, and fraud controls.

functional: Search properties and rates by location and dates, inspect policies, place a temporary hold, pay, and confirm a reservation.
Support cancellations, modifications, refunds, partner inventory updates, guest identity, and booking notifications.
Expose availability freshness, hold expiry, payment state, confirmation code, inventory audit, and reconciliation status.
nonFunctional: Never oversell a room inventory unit unless an explicit property overbooking policy permits it.
Handle high concurrency by partitioning inventory by property and date and isolating popular hotels and event dates.
Make holds, payment authorization, confirmation, cancellation, and partner callbacks idempotent.
Return a pending payment or unavailable state rather than confirming when inventory or processor state is uncertain.
scaleAssumptions: Search 10 million properties and process 100,000 booking attempts per minute during travel and event peaks.
Partition by property, room type, and stay date; isolate hot properties and aggregate search caches separately.
Retain inventory ledgers, holds, payments, confirmations, partner messages, and reconciliation evidence.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Hotel reservation platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Hotel reservation platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Hotel reservation platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Hotel reservation platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Hotel reservation platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Hotel reservation platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Hotel reservation platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Hotel reservation platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Hotel reservation platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
